newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil tells Heidrun oil buyers of delays.
newsitem.headline: Statoil tells Heidrun oil buyers of delays.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it would supply one more cargo of Heidrun crude from the Mongstad terminal, but the next delivery would depend on the unscheduled shutdown at the field.

Statoil shut in production on Wednesday at the 250,000 barrels per day Heidrun field after the flare tip fell off the platform. The tip is a safety measure for releasing pressure from the process facilities.
It was not immediately known how long the downtime will be.
"We have informed our customers of the problems at Heidrun and that we cannot supply according to the original plan," said Statoil spokeswoman Berit Rynning Oeyen.
"Those that need a replacement crude will be supplied, but so far we haven't had any response."

Oeyen said a shutdown of two to three days would not cause severe disruption to the loading schedule. Shuttle tankers deliver around 800,000 barrels of Heidrun oil to the Mongstad terminal every third day.
